title: Arithmetic fundamental group after a finite constant-field extension
statement: Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with fixed algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let $m\geq1$, and let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme in the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $X_0^{(m)}=X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ using the base-change construction [def-pc-base-change], regarded as an $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme. Then $X_0^{(m)}$ is connected. Choose a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ and give $X_0^{(m)}$ and $X_0$ the geometric points obtained by composing with $X\to X_0^{(m)}\to X_0$. The continuous homomorphism $\pi_1(X_0^{(m)},\bar x)\to\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)$ induced by the projection $X_0^{(m)}\to X_0$ [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] is injective and identifies the arithmetic étale fundamental group $\pi_1(X_0^{(m)})$ of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] with the inverse image of $\operatorname{Gal}(k/\mathbf F_{q^m})$ under the canonical projection $\pi_1(X_0)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$. Under this identification, the kernel of the projection to $\operatorname{Gal}(k/\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is the same geometric fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$ as for $X_0$.

proof.text: Write $L=\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $Y=X_0^{(m)}$, and $f:Y\to X_0$. By the definition of geometric connectedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], the base changes of $X_0$ to $k_0$, $L$, and $k$ are connected. In particular $X_0$, $Y$, and $X$ are connected. By the iterated-base-change identification in [def-pc-base-change], $Y\times_L k=X_0\times_{k_0}k=X$, with the same projections and the stipulated geometric points.

proof.text: The subfield $L\subset k$ has $q^m$ elements and contains $k_0$ by [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure]. Its elements form a finite spanning set over $k_0$, so $L/k_0$ is finite. For any finite subextension $E/k_0$ in $k$, a basis of length $d$ gives $Q=q^d$ elements in $E$. By [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card] every $\alpha\in E$ satisfies $\alpha^Q-\alpha=0$. This polynomial has derivative $-1$, so its minimal-polynomial divisor is coprime to its derivative; thus $E/k_0$ is separable in the definition [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. This applies to $L$. It also applies to $k_0(\alpha)$ for every $\alpha\in k$, since $k/k_0$ is algebraic, and powers below the minimal-polynomial degree span $k_0(\alpha)$. Consequently the given algebraic closure $k$ is also a separable closure of $k_0$. Finally $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is finite by the finite-module definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: arithmetic fundamental group under constant extension

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] to the finite separable extension $L/k_0$: $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is etale. Its pullback along $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is exactly $f:Y\to X_0$. It is finite by part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change].

Apply the finite-etale clause of [thm-galois-fundamental] to $f$, with the compatible geometric points from step 1. It gives the continuous injective map $f_*:\pi_1(Y,\bar x)\to G:=\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)$, whose image is the stabilizer of the marked point in the geometric fibre of $Y\to X_0$. Denote this marked point by $e$. Thus it remains to calculate its stabilizer, rather than to descend arbitrary covers of $Y$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: arithmetic fundamental group under constant extension

proof.text: Put $p:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and $r:G\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ for its canonical arithmetic map. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-base-change] identifies the fibre of $Y=p^*(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ at $\bar x$ with the $k_0$-embeddings $L\to\Omega$, where $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the chosen geometric point. The map $k\to\Omega$ comes from $\bar x\to X$. Since all roots of $T^{q^m}-T$ already lie in $k$ by [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure], these embeddings are exactly the embeddings $L\to k$ followed by $k\to\Omega$; $e$ corresponds to the fixed inclusion $L\subset k$. The equivariant fibre bijections of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] say that the $G$-action is the Galois action restricted along $r$. By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification], applied with the separable closure $k$ justified in step 2, the stabilizer of this inclusion in $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ is $\operatorname{Gal}(k/L)$. Hence $\operatorname{Stab}_G(e)=r^{-1}(\operatorname{Gal}(k/L))$. Together with step 4 this is the asserted image identification.

proof.text: Let $r_Y:\pi_1(Y)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/L)$ be the arithmetic map for $Y/L$. Composing the two structural projections to $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ gives $r\circ f_*=j\circ r_Y$, where $j:\operatorname{Gal}(k/L)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ is inclusion. Indeed, on each finite etale $k_0$-cover both maps act on its pullback fibre by the same natural automorphism; this is the equivariant pullback formula of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and equality of such automorphisms is componentwise equality by [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Since $j$ is injective, step 5 identifies $\ker r_Y$ with $r^{-1}(\operatorname{Gal}(k/L))\cap\ker r=\ker r$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: arithmetic fundamental group under constant extension

proof.text: Identify $\ker r$ geometrically using the kernel clause of [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] for $X_0$. By [def-wf-weil-group], $W(X_0)$ is the inverse image of the cyclic Frobenius subgroup and its degree records the exponent. Thus an element of $G$ with $r(g)=1$ belongs to $W(X_0)$ with degree zero; conversely an element of degree zero has $r(g)=1$. The cited exact sequence identifies this degree-zero subgroup, with its natural inclusion, with $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$. Therefore $\ker r=\pi_1(X)$, and step 6 identifies $\ker r_Y$ with that very subgroup. The identification respects the geometric map from $X$ because the projections $X\to Y\to X_0$ compose to the original projection and the geometric fibre equality in step 1 uses those projections.
